topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the lecturer and situates the lecture on cancer causation within the course before stating its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular conditions of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution when cellular susceptibility and the surrounding microenvironment permit it.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than attributing cancer solely to chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious influences.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on biological processing and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require subsequent promotion for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of exposure determines carcinogenic effects and conclude by consolidating the mechanisms of cancer causation discussed so far.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and why available investigative methods have important limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing recaps the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and carcinogen assessment while emphasizing everyday risk–benefit decisions.
